### Front line

Independent monitoring project DeepStateMap reported no territorial changes along the front line, recording 0 square kilometers of newly occupied or contested territory. The Economist’s war-fire model likewise registered zero war-related satellite fire detections. 

In contrast, the Russian Ministry of Defence claimed that its "Vostok" grouping captured the settlement of Tersyanka in Zaporizhzhia Oblast. The Russian ministry also reported localized tactical actions, claiming strikes against Ukrainian drone command positions, ammunition depots, and troop rotations in Zaporizhzhia and Kharkiv Oblasts. 

Meanwhile, open-source monitoring initiative GeoConfirmed verified four instances of Ukrainian short-range one-way attack drones targeting Russian assault groups in Donetsk Oblast.

### Strikes and losses

The Russian Ministry of Defence claimed a series of drone strikes against Ukrainian transport and energy infrastructure. According to the Russian military, these strikes hit an electrical substation in Pryluky (Chernihiv Oblast), two railway locomotives near Matviivka station (Zaporizhzhia Oblast), and two dry-cargo vessels allegedly transporting military cargo—one at sea heading toward Odesa and another docked at the port of Chornomorsk, where port facilities were also reportedly damaged. Regarding air defence, the Russian MoD claimed its units intercepted 68 Ukrainian fixed-wing drones across two waves over various regions, including Belgorod, Bryansk, Moscow, and Crimea, and shot down several Ukrainian drones over the battlefield. These claims remain unverified by independent sources.

The Ukrainian Ministry of Defence did not provide a daily breakdown of incoming strikes, but issued a summary claiming that over the past week, Ukrainian forces penetrated Russian air defence up to 2,500 km into Russian rear areas. Ukrainian officials claimed long-range strikes hit the Samara oil depot, three large refineries, an oil terminal at the port of Ust-Luga—allegedly setting fire to five reservoirs and a pier—as well as an Iskander missile fuel plant and drone launch bases.

### Official statements

The Ukrainian Ministry of Defence reported that Ukrainian Defence Minister Yevhen Khmara held bilateral talks with foreign defence leaders ahead of an upcoming Ramstein-format meeting:
* Speaking with UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting, Khmara discussed an upcoming military aid package, aircraft ammunition, rapid supplies of systems to defeat jet-powered drones, and joint defence manufacturing, noting that expanding partner defence-industrial capacity is a priority for 2027.
* In discussions with Canadian Defence Minister David McGuinty, Khmara acknowledged Canadian contributions to PAC-3 missile procurement and requested expedited deliveries of 20-mm ammunition for F-16 fighters, stating that these aircraft destroy the "lion's share" of Russian jet drones. Khmara also advocated for funding the direct procurement of Ukrainian-manufactured drones.

According to the Russian Ministry of Defence, Russian Deputy Defence Minister Dmitry Shcherbinin attended an artificial intelligence festival for military cadets, stating that modern personnel must understand, develop, and apply advanced technologies such as neural networks on the battlefield.
